basis: Prepared from the actual Old English in sources/audits/unit13-source/reading-source.json, checked public notes and the English context bridge. No source-editor, coordinator or other private translation was opened.
translation: When he was then doing something of this sort outside one day, and his companions were going to the town, to the church, as they often did, and the bishop, alone in the oratory, was intent either on reading or on prayers, he suddenly heard, as he afterwards said, the sweetest and most beautiful voice of people singing and rejoicing descending from heaven to earth.

He said that he first heard that voice and song from the southeastern part of heaven, that is, from the height of the winter sun’s rising; and from there they drew near to him little by little, until it reached the roof of the oratory in which the bishop was. Entering, it filled the whole place and surrounded it on every side.

He then directed his mind intently to the things that he heard. Then, after about half an hour, he again heard that same joyful song rising from the roof of the same oratory and returning up to heaven with indescribable sweetness by the same way by which it had come before.
Then he remained there for a while, wondering and marvelling; and with a thoughtful mind he considered and pondered what those things were to mean.

Then the bishop opened the window of the oratory and struck a signal with his hand, as was his custom if anyone was outside, so that the person should come in to him. Then he immediately went in to him. He, the bishop, said to him, ‘Go quickly to the church and tell our seven brothers to come here to me; and be present with them yourself as well.’
interpretive_notes: The opening and the attention/wondering clauses concern Owini. His companions are the plural subject of ēodon and dydon. Chad is the subject of wæs within the opening and of ontȳnde and slōg in the later sentence.
The fronted accusatives Ðā stefne and ðone sang are the objects of gehīerde inside the reported content, as note 8 expressly states. They are not accusative objects of cwæð.

Nēalǣcton is plural, continuing the coordinated voice and song; subsequent hē has the masculine sang as antecedent, expressly identified by note 9a. Neither hē becōm nor hē ǣr cōm should be translated as an unannounced journey by Owini or Chad.

Eall is accusative singular according to note 12; the English whole place is an interpretive rendering of the place filled. The exact force and implied object of in ymbhwyrfte ymbsealde need final lexical reconciliation; on every side expresses the spatial scope without inventing a new actor.
The reported perception at the half-hour point has the accusative song with infinitives ūpāstīgan and ęfthweorfan. The intervening relative identifies its earlier path.
Hwæt ðā ðing bēon sceolden concerns the meaning or significance of the events, not an assertion that future events would necessarily occur.

The customary signal and its condition are explanatory background; the final ðæt clause gives the intended response. The source’s subsequent hē is Owini, then hē, se bisceop explicitly identifies Chad as the speaker.

The final ūre is the bishop’s first-person plural possessive, mē refers to Chad, and ðū addresses Owini. Seven brothers are summoned and Owini is to be present as well. The two church locations must be distinguished through note 5 and the context bridge.
open_reconciliation_points: Check the exact lexical scope of in ymbhwyrfte ymbsealde and whether filled everything, filled the entire building or another rendering is most transparent with the retained local help.
Check the most natural English rendering of mid wes while preserving its accompanying/present sense and the source’s explicit inclusion of Owini.
